column2: Fifty-nine seconds. That's how long the first real flight lasted. Getting there took everything.
At the time, only madmen tried to fly. The papers said it was a million years away.
Bedridden for years, Wilbur Wright read everything about birds, and followed the logic all the way to himself.
They needed a wing that could lift a man. So they built their own wind tunnel, and tested shape after shape.
No engine on the market was light enough. So they did the maths, and built one themselves.
Then came four years of crashed gliders and failed calculations. Even Wilbur gave up, for one night.
December seventeenth, nineteen-oh-three. Two men the locals called nuts lifted off a beach, and stayed up for fifty-nine seconds.
Last year, airlines flew five point five eight billion seats. It all traces back to that beach.
Clear thinking. A bias to action. And the nerve to disagree. That's high agency, and you can learn it.
